correctness.rationale: For an all-negative clique, each monochromatic set-partition block must receive a different magnitude and may choose either sign; this gives the Stirling expansion and (2exp(z)−1)^(q/2) EGF at even q, then formally at any q by polynomial interpolation coefficient by coefficient. Orienting the bridge-only attachments away from the core gives a q−1 factor per added vertex regardless of sign. Thus for r=0 the t³ coefficient is 2−(n+1)E_n(1), and for r≥1 the first nonzero coefficient is 2 at t³ and the t⁴ coefficient is 2^r E_n(3)−2(n+r+1). The EGF binomial expansions and all derivatives converge absolutely in a neighborhood of zero. At q=1 and odd n, every summand in the derivative expansion is positive, so E_n(1)≥1 by the integer-coefficient Stirling formula. At q=3 and odd n, only j=0 gives a positive summand. The exact terms j=3,…,8 already outweigh it at n=7 (ratio 731229629/679477248); their relative bases are all ≥1, so they do so for every odd n≥7. The two bridge base numerators at n=3 and 5 were independently reproduced in exact arithmetic. A further bridge acts by t d/dt−2 on the original series; clearing the new denominator gives h̃_i=(i−2)h_i+(N+4−i)h_{i−1}. Here h₀=h₁=h₂=0 and deg H≤N+1 by the vanishing of polynomial finite differences above order N, so both multipliers are nonnegative at every relevant index including the new last index N+2. This proves the full classification, not just the sampled orders.
residual_risks: Odd-q values are formal evaluations, not odd-palette counts. The infinite sign and positivity conclusions use the analytic argument and recurrence, not truncation of a computational sample.

evidence: Theorem 1.1 characterizes positivity by balanced blocks for connected signed graphs that admit a balancing vertex; it covers the whole n=3 subfamily. At n≥5 deletion of any one vertex leaves an unbalanced negative clique triangle.
Proposition 3.1 records the known all-negative-clique enumeration. Lemma 2.1(a) gives the gluing factor used to produce (q−1)^r.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Theorem 1.1 cannot be applied using a balanced bridge alone when there is no balancing vertex. The enumeration and product allow calculating a fixed instance but are not a sign classification across all orders and attachments.

value.rationale: For cores beyond the theorem requiring a balancing vertex, it gives a complete and sharp odd-clique cutoff in a natural family of arbitrary balanced bridge attachments. The n≥7 negative fourth coefficient is a stable obstruction to repair by any number or shape of those attachments, and K₅ gives a positive no-balancing-vertex counterpart. The contribution is not the prior triangle calculation or mere evaluation of a polynomial at one order.
residual_risks: No even-clique, general signed graph, nonbridge attachment or real-rootedness conclusion.
